The '''Kwa Holdings''' were an interstellar benevolent empire in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] during the [[Pre-Republic era]]. It was dominated by the saurian [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]] of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] whom had mastered [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] which they called the Power of the Cosmos. 

==History==
During the [[Pre-Republic era]] the [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]] were a warm-blooded reptilian species that developed intelligence on [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]]. The Kwa were strong in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], which they called the Power of the Cosmos. The Kwa connection with the Power of the Cosmos allowed them to create the [[Infinity Gate|Infinity Gates]] which enabled instantaneous travel and could double as [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]] since they were modeled on [[Celestial/Legends|Celestial]] concepts.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

[[File:Iktotch_Kwa.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Kwa visited many species such as the primitive Iktotchi.]]
At some point during the reign of the Kwa, they came into contact with the [[Gree]] who had their own from of teleportation called [[hypergate|hypergates]]. The energy outputs generated by the Gree hypergates and the Celestial-derived Infinity Gates provoked a territorial rivalry between the Gree and the Kwa, culminating in a millennia-spanning [[Gree-Kwa conflict|war]] that endured until approximately the period in which the [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronians]] and [[Gossam/Legends|Gossams]] conducted their early [[Tumbledrive/Legends|tumble hyperdrive]] experiments around [[27,000 BBY/Legends|27,000 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" />

According to the Kwa male [[A'nang]], the Kwa brought civilization to the cultures that the Kwa came across.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 3">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 3|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 3]]</ref> The Kwa had a pattern of sharing their technology with the peoples they came across. This would be the Kwa's undoing when they visited [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]] where they encountered the primitive [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]]. This resulted in the Rakata learning the Force and obtaining the advanced technology. In time, the Kwa realized they had made a grave mistake, having failed to recognize the Rakata’s true, destructive nature.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 4">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 4|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 4]]</ref>

==Astrography==
The Kwa territorial holdings encompassed the worlds of [[Salin]] and [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]].<ref name="TEA" /> The Kwa also had visited [[Iktotch/Legends|Iktotch]] and had a lived on [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] for sometime, describing Tython as their Home as well.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 3" />

==Legacy==
[[File:Kwa-holocron.png|thumb|left|250px|The Holocron of A'nang is activated by Je'daii Journeyer, Tasha Ryo.]]
In [[25,793 BBY]] the  [[Holocron of A'nang]], which was constructed by the ancient Kwa [[A'nang]], was activated by [[Je'daii Journeyer]], [[Tasha Ryo]]. In the Holocron the A'nang descibed the past of the Kwa and their empire.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 3" />

When [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] was imprisoned on Dathomir as a slave by the [[Nightsisters]] of Dathomir he communed with a [[Kwi]], a devolved species descended of the Kwa, communed with Vos through the force.<ref name="SWIE2">[[Star Wars (1998) 24|''Star Wars'' (1998) 24]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Kwa Holdings were first developed for the [[2000]] [[Star Wars comic books|Comic]] [[Star Wars (1998) 24|''Star Wars'' (1998) 24]] by writer [[Pat Mills]].<ref name="SWIE2" /> They were first referred to with the title in [[The Essential Atlas]] written by [[Jason Fry]] and published in [[2009]]<ref name="TEA" />
